Allow customisation of child logger bindings (or the instance itself) via child logger factory function.

Closes #4751 

#### Checklist

pr_comments:
Referring to https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/4751#issuecomment-1548582144, not sure if we should also do a `fastify.setChildLoggerFactory` instance method to allow it to be set/encapsulated by a plugin?

If so, not sure if there's anything special I have to do to allow encapsulation etc...

On my side, I think it can be an interesting addition, especially for plugins to have capabilities to also maybe decorate the logger with extra properties (e.g. `traceId`, custom headers, etc.)

Though, I would like to hear from @fastify/core their thoughts 🙂
We use tsd for testing the types
Added the type check in the last commit

If we want to add `fastify.setChildLoggerFactory()` for encapsulation, then I need some guidance. Really not sure where to begin so need some hints. Do I just add the method to the root `fastify` object returned from the constructor?

>If we want to add fastify.setChildLoggerFactory() for encapsulation, then I need some guidance. Really not sure where to begin so need some hints. Do I just add the method to the root fastify object returned from the constructor?

To achieve this we need to do the following:
1. We will need to define a default `childLoggerFactory` fn when instantiating [`fastify`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/e82f4a7d463e49c5b9b33011a590979e872c4571/fastify.js#L226). We need hide the child logger fn behind a symbol.
2. We need to define it within the [`Context`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/e82f4a7d463e49c5b9b33011a590979e872c4571/lib/context.js#L21) object. It should use the one attached to `fastify` at the previous step using the symbol.
3. The `fastify.setChildLoggerFactory` should modify the default child logger fn hidden with the symbol, so the `context` object can reference it within nested encapsulations. e.g. [`setSerializerCompiler`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/fastify.js#L754)

Let me know if I had something wrong or if any doubt 😄 

> **Update**

Sorry, missed the last part 😅 
4. On the `createChildLogger` fn, you'll need to access the `context` for the child logger fn to create the new logger. Of course, using the symbol from step 1

Ok I added encapsulation per-plugin and per-route, like `errorHandler` etc. And it looks like I've done it right because I added tests similar to `errorHandler` and it seems to be working. Let me know your thoughts.

My only note is: configuration options like `errorHandler` which have a `setErrorHandler()` funciton on the fastify instance don't currently also have a constructor option. However for the child logger factory we have both the `childLoggerFactory` constructor option, and the `setChildLoggerFactory` option. Do we remove the constructor option now or keep both?

So sorry guys, I posted a whole bunch of comments several weeks ago and didn't realise I had to submit the review for them to appear 🤦🏼

1. @metcoder95 a need your clarification here (https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4760#discussion_r1206962134)
2. @metcoder95 I implemented your suggestion (https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4760#discussion_r1206958652) but it had a couple of implications (https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4760#discussion_r1207570420, https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4760#discussion_r1207572291) which seem benign but need you to confirm.
3. Need consensus on whether, now that we have added instance method `setChildLoggerFactory`, we should remove the `childLoggerFactory` constructor option or not.

issue_context.title: Feature: Child logger hook
comments: Thanks for reporting! Would you like to send a Pull Request to address this issue? Remember to add unit tests.
This could be a nice option for the Fastify constructor.

>For the use case I personally have in mind, a global configuration will be fine because it depends only on the platform that the app runs on. However, I guess it is conceivable that different plugins/routes may receive requests from different platforms which may need to parse bindings in different ways? Or maybe that's overcomplicating it.

The `fastify` constructor seems enough, as anyways it passes the `request` object that can be used to retrieve the data out of it to create the child logger. On top, maybe an API like `fastify.setChildLoggerFactory` (the name is just a suggestion, might not be best 😅) can help this be used as well by a `plugin` if any. 

Not so sure if it really deserves its own lifecycle-hook 🤔
@metcoder95 @mcollina before I go too far on the PR, do you have a preference between options 1/2 above?

>@metcoder95 @mcollina before I go too far on the PR, do you have a preference between options 1/2 above?

Option 2 seems to offer the best flexibility and ergonomics. In that way, the child logger instantiation can be customized at full if wished 👍

review_comments: Same thing, `onBadUrlContext` used by `new Request()` below was a "dummy" context in the global scope, now it is a proper context. `onSend` and `onError` were `[]` and now they are `null` (set inside the `Context` constructor)... Tests seem to pass...

It was because the `badUrl` is handled differently than other cases. For instance, it creates the `Request` and `Reply` objects if the `frameworkErrors` hanlder is passed when creating the fastify app.

It shouldn't have negative impact, but we can ask @mcollina for a second pair of eyes to verify

`fourOhFourContext ` (used by `new Request()` below) was previously a "dummy" context in the global scope. Now it is the proper scoped context. Was there a reason it was done that way? Is it ok to change this? Tests seem to pass.
This has the same goal as https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4760#discussion_r1236584946 but for the `onBadUrlHandler` instead
